newsitem.title: UK: Pearson drops on CEO, Sky stake gloom.
newsitem.headline: Pearson drops on CEO, Sky stake gloom.

text.p: Shares in Pearson dropped on Thursday in a firm market on disappointment about its new chief executive and worries about the media group's plans to sell its stake in broadcaster BSkyB, dealers said.
Pearson shares were down 16-1/2p or 2.4 percent at 671-1/2p. Over 830,000 shares had changed hands by 0800 GMT.
Dealers said investors had been disappointed Marjorie Scardino's appointment as chief executive at Pearson. She succeeds Frank Barlow at the end of the year.
"The market was looking for a big hitter and she wasn't the big name it was looking for," one market maker said.

That was echoed by other dealers who said the market had also worried about a report in the Independent newspaper, which said Pearson had resolved concerns about the tax implications of selling its BSkyB stake but faced difficulties separating the direct and indirect holdings.
The report said Pearson's indirect stake of around four percent is worth 440 million stg at BSkyB's current share price.
Jason Crisp, media analyst at SocGen in London, said he was surprised at concern about the Sky stake sale plans.
"We would see this as a fairly rational thing to do and are recommending people take profits after its recent run," he said.
But he said the concerns about Scardino were understandable.
"The market really doesn't know who she is. She's not such a well known name and I think that's the problem," he said.

Nick Ward, media analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing, said it was good news that the appointments had been made now and that Dennis Stevenson -- "a high calibre manager and well thought of" -- would take over as deputy chairman immediately at Pearson.
Stevenson takes over as chairman from May next year.
"But the downside is that the City was looking for a big-branded name for CEO who would have the clout to sort things, however good Scardino is," Ward said.
"It could now be much harder for her," Ward said.
Ward said he was maintaining his "buy" recommendation on Pearson shares.

"But we are now in a situation where, instead of getting a big jump in the share price and discounting ahead of things to come, things will have to happen at Pearson before the share price will move," he said.
